thread:
alex: FYI i'm seeing weird "sloshing" in paged-attn experiments on the 32k convo workload. p99 token latency spikes correlate with bursts of page evictions. attaching quick snapshot below.

maria: @alex can you paste the allocator dump? curious if it's fragmentation vs eviction policy. :thinking:

alex: sure — shortened alloc dump:
```
alloc_stats:
  pages_total: 2048
  pages_free: 28
  pages_reserved_hot: 12
  evictions_per_min: 270
  avg_eviction_write_us: 310
  page_faults/sec: 3.7
  kv_cache_util_pct: 87
```

sachin: interesting. that avg_eviction_write_us looks high. could be write amplification from scattered slotmap holes — when a hot prefix migrates we end up copying many small spans. any pattern in page sizes?

alex: mostly 64KB pages, but we also have mixed 16k/64k due to fallback from small allocations. noticed fragmentation histogram skewed: many tiny free ranges.

remi: i ran a quick microbench this morning: fused-attn variant keeps steady throughput up to 8k context, >16k the paged-attn path sees tail regressions. suspecting KV pager contention + cuda sync points triggered by our async fallback. results:
```
bench: paged-vs-fused (1xA100)
  seq=8k: fused p50=45ms p99=120ms, paged p50=60ms p99=180ms
  seq=16k: fused p50=85ms p99=240ms, paged p50=120ms p99=760ms
  seq=32k: fused p50=220ms p99=610ms, paged p50=900ms p99=2.8s
```

maria: those deltas scream pager-induced syncs. we should double-check kernel selection path: are we forcing FlashAttn-2 for long context and falling back to a slower kernel when KV hits a page fault?

alex: yes, routing picks flash2 for <16k, and paged-attn kernels for >16k. but the pager is invoked by the runtime when KV misses on GPU memory and moves pages in via host->device copies. that copy triggers stream sync in a few places.

sachin: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) prefetch strategy for active prefixes (maintain a tiny working set pinned for the current batch), 2) hysteresis in eviction so we don't oscillate (i.e., don't evict until free_pages < X and then free to Y). both are relatively cheap to prototype.

remi: also try cooperative backpressure at batching layer: if page_faults/sec > T, reduce batch size or prefer shorter sequences for that worker. this avoids waterfalling into more faults.

alex: i'm going to try a pinned-hotset experiment: pin last N prefixes for current request set and force pager to avoid those pages. will run perf-bot job.

perf-bot: perf run queued: run_id=pr-6912, config=pinned-hotset-N=16, target=32k-convos. link: https://ci.internal/perf/pr-6912 :robot_face:

maria: nice. also add a metric for "evictions_causing_sync" — whether the eviction path blocked the main stream vs being async. helps differentiate kernel vs pager behavior.

alex: good call. i'll include that. initial hypothesis: allocator fragmentation + aggressive LRU admission is causing frequent writebacks, which in turn forces kernels to sync and pick non-optimized paths.

sachin: if pinned-hotset helps, upstream follow-ups: (a) change allocator to buddy-ish for mixed sizes, (b) add admission control to reducer cold pages, (c) adjust kernel selection to prefer fused-attn when pager pressure is high.

remi: agree. one more note — check GPU CRC or PCIe saturation during these spikes (seen a few times where memcopy bursts saturate PCIe and everything staggers).

alex: thanks all. i'll post the perf run results here when done and attach the flame graphs. planning the first experiment tonight. :thumbsup:
